seoTitle: How to Put a YouTube Video in a Canva Presentation
metaDescription: Embed a YouTube video directly into your Canva presentation slides so it plays inline during a live presentation, no downloads required.
intro: Instead of downloading a video file to include in your slides, you can stream YouTube content directly inside a Canva presentation using its app integrations. This guide covers copying the video link, embedding it with Canva's YouTube or Embeds tool, and testing playback in presenter mode.

steps.heading: Copy the YouTube video URL
steps.body: On YouTube, use the Share option to copy the sharing link for your target video clip.

steps.heading: Prepare a blank slide
steps.body: Open your presentation project in Canva and set up a blank slide for the video.

steps.heading: Open the Apps section
steps.body: Navigate to the Apps tab on the left-hand sidebar of the editor.

steps.heading: Find the YouTube or Embeds tool
steps.body: Search for the native YouTube app or the core Embeds utility and paste your video link into the input field.

steps.heading: Resize and position the video
steps.body: Scale and arrange the video element on your slide canvas so it fits your layout.

steps.heading: Test playback in Presenter View
steps.body: Preview your slide deck to confirm the video plays inline and controls respond correctly during a live presentation.

faq.question: Do I need to download the video file first?
faq.answer: No, the whole point of this method is streaming the video directly from YouTube without downloading anything.

faq.question: Will the video play automatically during my presentation?
faq.answer: Playback typically requires a click to start, so it's worth testing in Presenter View beforehand to know exactly when to trigger it.

faq.question: Can I use this with a private or unlisted YouTube video?
faq.answer: The embed relies on the video's sharing link, so accessibility depends on the video's privacy settings on YouTube.

faq.question: Will the embedded video work if I export the presentation to PDF?
faq.answer: Interactive video embeds are designed for live, on-screen presentations and generally won't function as playable video inside a static PDF export.
